fields.description: The engine/discipline this item master row belongs to (e.g. 'Electrical'). Discipline-wide: items are addressed by (discipline, kind), NOT by category_id -- the per-category config lives in BoQ Rate Category Config. Stamped from the import payload's category_config.discipline.
fields.label: Discipline

fields.description: The item kind within the discipline (e.g. 'cable', 'termination'). Part of the composite read index [discipline, kind, brand]; the read endpoint filters on (discipline, optional kind).
fields.label: Kind

fields.description: Manufacturer brand (e.g. 'Polycab'). A day-one dimension; becomes a selector when multi-brand data loads. NOT a normalized attribute -- stored verbatim.
fields.label: Brand

fields.description: Unit of measure for this item (e.g. 'Mtr' for cable, 'Set' for termination).
fields.label: Unit

fields.description: Opaque keyed attribute map used to match a master row for the selected line (e.g. {material, insulation, core, thickness_sqmm}). JSON (not exploded columns / child table) per the app's stated rule: flexible, UI-driven, read-whole data. Material/insulation values are CANONICAL UPPERCASE (normalized at import); matching downstream is EXACT on canonical values.
fields.label: Attributes

fields.description: Opaque keyed rate map -- the raw list/base rates this row supplies to the category's derivation pipelines (e.g. cable: {list_price_per_mtr, install_base_per_mtr}; termination: {lug_list, gland_band1_list, gland_band2_list}). JSON per the same rule; the pipelines (stored in BoQ Rate Category Config) interpret these.
fields.label: Rates

fields.description: The source workbook sheet this row was extracted from (e.g. 'Wiring & cabling', 'Termination').
fields.label: Source Sheet

fields.description: The 1-based source row within the source sheet. With source_sheet, gives a faithful back-pointer to the origin workbook cell block.
fields.label: Source Row

fields.description: One shared batch id per import event (prefix 'rmbulk-'), stamped on every row loaded together -- mirrors BoQ Category Truth Snapshot's gtbulk batch-provenance. A --replace re-import deactivates the prior batch and mints a new one (freeze-and-supersede; rows are never deleted).
fields.label: Import Batch

fields.description: Whether this row is the live/current version. A --replace re-import sets active=0 on the prior batch. Read endpoints return active rows ONLY.
fields.label: Active

fields.description: STABLE, DURABLE row identity across mints -- the handle a CSV round trip (download -> edit -> upload) matches on. STAMPED (opaque), never derived from content: a content hash would CHANGE when an attribute is edited, so an edited row would return with a different id, read as an insert, and leave the original active -- a silent duplicate on every rename, which is the exact failure this field exists to prevent. `name` CANNOT serve: freeze-and-supersede RETAINS the superseded row, so its name stays occupied and a new row reusing it is a primary-key collision. NOT UNIQUE on this table -- unique only among active=1 rows; every superseded version of an item legitimately shares its uid, which is what makes history traceable. Backfilled on ACTIVE rows only (owner ruling): a superseded row has no reliable key to its successor, since the only handle is content and content is what changes between versions.
fields.label: Item UID
